SMTO-MON-0008 — This monitor has no command to run

GUID: f2ab325a-3d7f-4d5f-aeed-e4578f48f6a7
Slug: monitor-command-empty
Domain: MON · Subsystem: mon

What happened

  • The monitor's command was blank, so SMTO had nothing to run and didn't create the monitor.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the agent to start the monitor again with the exact command in backticks, for example free -m. A monitor works by running a command over and over, so it can't exist without one.
  2. If you don't know the command, describe what to watch, such as free disk space or GPU memory, and ask the agent for a read-only command. SMTO recognizes common checks like disk, memory and GPU and can fill in a suitable command.

What success looks like

  • The agent reports the monitor started and shows the command it runs.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resend the request without a command; it will be rejected the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • monitor_command_rejection_reason rejected the monitor because the normalized command is empty.

What this means

  • Monitor command normalization produces an empty string before safety inspection. Monitor validation does not execute the observation command. Existing monitor state and stored observations remain authoritative; missing planning support or exhausted judgment budget does not prove observation collection failed.

Why this can happen

  • Monitor command normalization produces an empty string before safety inspection.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the normalized command field, including whitespace-only input.

How to fix it

  • Provide a nonblank, noninteractive observation command in the create payload or the monitor.start arguments; see monitor_command_rejection_reason in src/agent_runtime/monitors/drafting.py.
  • Supply the intended noninteractive observation command.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate nonempty observation command reaches normal safety validation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Monitor validation does not execute the observation command. Existing monitor state and stored observations remain authoritative; missing planning support or exhausted judgment budget does not prove observation collection failed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
